interface_and_flux_interpretation.observation: Fortran rpn2 returns two waves, two speeds and three-component negative/positive fluctuations amdq/apdq. The conserved components are depth, x momentum and y momentum. This file is a normal Riemann interface routine, not a complete two-dimensional time advance.

Gravity comes from the cparam common block. For ixy=1, normal momentum is component2 and tangential momentum component3; the other direction exchanges them. A later standalone NumPy method must rotate both input/output momentum roles consistently.

At interface i, the left state is qr(:,i-1), and the right state is ql(:,i). The code divides momenta by depth and takes square roots directly. It forms h_hat=(hL+hR)/2 and sqrt(h)-weighted normal u_hat, with c_hat=sqrt(g*h_hat). Positive finite depth and valid gravity are assumptions; this file supplies no dry-state guards.

The speeds are sL=min(uL-cL,u_hat-c_hat) and sR=max(uR+cR,u_hat+c_hat). The middle state includes depth, normal momentum and tangential momentum, so a two-state h/normal-q adaptation would discard a required conservative component.
The two wave jumps sum to the full three-state difference. Each speed times its wave contributes to amdq for negative speed, or apdq otherwise; zero-speed contribution is zero.

algebraic_flux_translation_for_a_future_.status: Source-based algebraic interpretation, not implemented or numerically compared in this preflight.
algebraic_flux_translation_for_a_future_.normal_physical_flux: For U=(h,q_n,q_t), F_n(U)=(q_n,q_n^2/h + g*h^2/2,q_n*q_t/h). Rotate this vector back for a y face.
algebraic_flux_translation_for_a_future_.HLL_middle_state: U_star=(sR*UR-sL*UL-(F_R-F_L))/(sR-sL), equivalent to the three component middle-state expressions in preserved lines72-74.
algebraic_flux_translation_for_a_future_.conservative_flux: Use F_L when sL>=0, F_R when sR<=0, and (sR*F_L-sL*F_R+sL*sR*(UR-UL))/(sR-sL) when the speeds straddle zero. Source fluctuations correspond to F_star=F_L+amdq=F_R-apdq. The existing predeclared reference tests would need to verify a future implementation, including full tangential transport.
algebraic_flux_translation_for_a_future_.important_distinction: Do not label amdq or apdq alone as the boundary numerical flux. They are one-sided fluctuations; the physical flux term is needed for conservative wall and budget accounting.

what_this_source_does_not_establish: It does not specify the proposed unsplit forward-Euler Cartesian update, summed directional CFL cap, snapshot schedule, wall ghost states, exact rectangular initial averages or conservative area projection. Those remain separately documented local design choices.
It does not validate positivity for the proposed run, guarantee a boundary-safe horizon, supply refinement errors or establish reference accuracy.
It includes no bed, Manning friction, rainfall, wet/dry treatment or dry-state validation in this routine.
It does not establish a measured M5 runtime, memory budget, a neural solution or successful genuine 2D comparison.
